2026-11-13.g1: 📚 Quick Notes – P6 Financial Accounting Maturity of bills – 3 rules • Due date = date of bill + term + 3 days of grace. • Term in months → count calendar months (10 Jan + 3 months = 10 Apr → due 13 Apr). • Term in days → exclude the date of drawing. • Bills payable on demand/at sight → no days of grace. • Due date on a public holiday → preceding business day. 🔗 Linked to today's MCQ: Bill of exchange – due date 💪 One concept a day = 300+ concepts by exam day. Keep building strong CMA Inter concepts!
2026-11-13.g2: 📚 Formula Sheet – P12 Management Accounting CVP formulas in one place • P/V ratio = Contribution ÷ Sales. • BEP (₹) = Fixed cost ÷ P/V ratio. • Sales for desired profit = (Fixed cost + Desired profit) ÷ P/V ratio. • Margin of safety = Actual sales − BEP sales. • Profit = Margin of safety × P/V ratio. 🔗 Linked to today's MCQ: Sales for desired profit 💪 Future CMA, this is how toppers revise – one clear concept at a time.

2026-11-14.g1: 📚 Quick Notes – P7A Direct Taxation Gifts – when are they taxable? • Money received without consideration from non-relatives is taxable if the aggregate in the year exceeds ₹50,000 – then the WHOLE amount is taxable. • Fully exempt: gifts from relatives (spouse, brother/sister, brother/sister of spouse, brother/sister of parents, lineal ascendants/descendants and their spouses, etc.). • Also exempt: gifts on the occasion of marriage, and receipts under a will or by inheritance. 🔗 Linked to today's MCQ: Gifts from non-relatives 💪 Cost, control, compliance – a CMA masters all three. Today you mastered one more concept.
2026-11-14.g2: 📚 Cheat Sheet – P11A Financial Management Liquidity ratios • Current ratio = Current assets ÷ Current liabilities. • Quick ratio = (Current assets − Inventory − Prepaid expenses) ÷ Current liabilities. • Net working capital = Current assets − Current liabilities. • Shortcut: if Current ratio = r and NWC = W, then CL = W ÷ (r − 1) and CA = r × CL. 🔗 Linked to today's MCQ: Current ratio 💪 Dec 2026 is calling. Stay consistent, stay CMA-focused!

2026-11-16.g1: 📚 Formula Sheet – P8 Cost Accounting Labour turnover – 3 methods • Separation method = Separations ÷ Average workers × 100. • Replacement method = Replacements ÷ Average workers × 100. • Flux method = (Separations + Replacements) ÷ Average workers × 100. • Average workers = (Opening + Closing) ÷ 2. 🔗 Linked to today's MCQ: Labour turnover 💪 Every concept you learn adds value – just like a CMA adds value to every business.
2026-11-16.g2: 📚 Concept Clarity – P10B Auditing Internal check vs internal control vs internal audit • Internal check: division of work so that one person's work is automatically checked by another. • Internal audit: an independent review of operations and records, done after the work by internal auditors. • Internal control: the wider system of policies and procedures adopted by management – internal check and internal audit are parts of it. 🔗 Linked to today's MCQ: Internal check 💪 Believe in your preparation – the CMA designation rewards consistent effort.

2026-11-17.g1: 📚 Quick Notes – P7A Direct Taxation Composite income – business portion • Tea grown and manufactured: 40% business income, 60% agricultural. • Rubber: 35% business income, 65% agricultural. • Coffee grown and cured: 25% business income, 75% agricultural. • Coffee grown, cured, roasted and grounded: 40% business income, 60% agricultural. 🔗 Linked to today's MCQ: Tea – composite income 💪 One concept a day = 300+ concepts by exam day. Keep building strong CMA Inter concepts!
2026-11-17.g2: 📚 Concept Clarity – P9A Operations Management Critical path and float • Critical path = the longest path through the network; it gives the project duration. • Total float = Latest start − Earliest start (or Latest finish − Earliest finish). • Free float = Earliest start of the next activity − Earliest finish of this activity. • Activities on the critical path have zero total float. 🔗 Linked to today's MCQ: Network analysis – slack 💪 Future CMA, this is how toppers revise – one clear concept at a time.

2026-11-13.g1: 💡 Fun Fact – ICMAI's journey The Institute was first set up in 1944 as a company, and became a statutory body under the Cost and Works Accountants Act, 1959. It got its present name, The Institute of Cost Accountants of India, in 2012. Source: ICMAI – History of the Institute
2026-11-13.g2: 💡 Fun Fact – Cost audit is a CMA's domain Under Sec 148 of the Companies Act, 2013, cost audit can be conducted only by a Cost Accountant (CMA) – a professional area reserved for CMAs. Source: Companies Act, 2013 – Sec 148

2026-11-14.g1: 📝 Study Tip – Laws: section + example Learn every legal provision as 'rule + one exam-style example'. In MCQs the example decides the answer, not the section number. 💪 Every CMA you admire once sat with the same MCQs – keep going, your CMA tag is closer than you think.
2026-11-14.g2: 📝 Study Tip – OM: practise the numbers Capacity, productivity and network questions are pure calculation – do 5 sums a day instead of only reading the theory. 💪 A CMA is trusted with a company's costs – start by trusting your own daily routine.

2026-11-16.g1: 💡 Fun Fact – 500+ years of double entry Double-entry book-keeping was first described in print by the Italian mathematician Luca Pacioli in 1494 – the same system you use in every journal entry today. Source: Luca Pacioli, Summa de Arithmetica (1494)
2026-11-16.g2: 💡 Fun Fact – The Balanced Scorecard story Robert Kaplan and David Norton introduced the Balanced Scorecard in a 1992 Harvard Business Review article. It is now used by organisations worldwide. Source: Harvard Business Review, 1992

2026-11-17.g1: 📝 Study Tip – Accounts: write the formula first Before solving any FA sum, write the formula or account format in one line. It prevents silly mistakes under exam pressure. 💪 Cost Accountants measure every rupee; measure every study hour the same way.
2026-11-17.g2: 📝 Study Tip – Corporate Accounting: revise formats Keep one page with the Schedule III format and the redemption/buy-back entries. Revise it every Sunday. 💪 Dec 2026 is not far – one focused hour today is one step closer to 'CMA' before your name.

2026-11-18.g1: 💡 Fun Fact – Older than most laws you study The Indian Contract Act, 1872 came into force on 1 September 1872 – over 150 years ago – and still governs everyday contracts. Source: Indian Contract Act, 1872
2026-11-18.g2: 💡 Fun Fact – PERT and the Polaris missile PERT was developed in 1958 for the US Navy's Polaris missile project, and CPM was developed around the same time at DuPont. Both are in your network analysis chapter. Source: History of PERT/CPM

2026-11-19.g1: 📝 Study Tip – Tax: make a 1-page limit sheet Put all exemption limits, rates and day-count rules on one page and read it daily for 5 minutes. 💪 Discipline today, CMA tomorrow. Small steps, big designation!
2026-11-19.g2: 📝 Study Tip – FM: understand, don't memorise For every FM formula, ask 'why does this make sense?' If you understand the logic, you can rebuild the formula in the exam. 💪 Industry needs CMAs who understand numbers deeply – you are building that skill right now.

2026-11-20.g1: 💡 Fun Fact – GST's midnight launch GST was launched in India at a special midnight session of Parliament on 1 July 2017, replacing many central and state indirect taxes. Source: GST Council / Government of India
2026-11-20.g2: 💡 Fun Fact – Two Nobel prizes from one theory Franco Modigliani (1985) and Merton Miller (1990) both won the Nobel Prize in Economics. Their 1958 M–M theory of capital structure is in your FM syllabus. Source: Nobel Prize records

2026-11-21.g1: 📝 Study Tip – Costing: link theory with sums After each costing chapter, solve 2 theory MCQs and 2 numerical MCQs. CMA papers mix both. 💪 Clear Inter, then Final – every MCQ you solve today is a brick in your CMA career.
2026-11-21.g2: 📝 Study Tip – SM: use keywords Strategy answers score with the right keywords (SWOT, BCG, Ansoff, BSC). Underline them in your notes. 💪 Strategy wins exams too – plan your revision like a CMA plans a budget.

2026-11-23.g1: 💡 Fun Fact – Income tax since 1860 Income tax was first introduced in India in 1860 by Sir James Wilson to meet losses after the 1857 revolt. Source: Income Tax Department – History
2026-11-23.g2: 💡 Fun Fact – ABC is younger than you think Activity-based costing was popularised by Robert Kaplan and Robin Cooper in the late 1980s, when overheads became too large to allocate on labour hours alone. Source: Kaplan & Cooper, Harvard Business School

2026-11-24.g1: 📝 Study Tip – Attempt MCQs before reading the answer Always answer the daily MCQs on your own before checking. Mark the ones you got wrong and revise them on Saturday. 💪 Mistakes in practice cost nothing; mistakes in the exam cost an attempt. Practise now!
2026-11-24.g2: 📝 Study Tip – Audit: know the 'who can and cannot' Many audit MCQs test eligibility, prohibited services and appointment timelines. Make a table of these. 💪 Only a CMA can sign a cost audit report – aim for that signature, one chapter at a time.

2026-11-25.g1: 💡 Fun Fact – Sale of Goods was once Contract Act The rules on sale of goods were originally Chapter VII of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. They were separated into the Sale of Goods Act, 1930. Source: Sale of Goods Act, 1930
2026-11-25.g2: 💡 Fun Fact – XBRL filing in India The Ministry of Corporate Affairs made XBRL filing of financial statements mandatory for certain classes of companies starting with FY 2010-11. Source: MCA – XBRL filing

2026-11-26.g2: 📝 Study Tip – Management Accounting: check units In CVP and budgets, always check whether the answer is in units or ₹. Many wrong options differ only in units. 💪 Your CMA journey is a long-term investment – today's effort is the best return you can earn.

2026-11-13.g1: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P5 Business Laws Essentials of a valid contract • A contract is an agreement enforceable by law (Indian Contract Act, 1872 – Sec 2(h)). All agreements are not contracts. • Essentials: (1) offer and acceptance, (2) intention to create legal relations, (3) lawful consideration, (4) capacity of parties, (5) free consent, (6) lawful object, (7) not expressly declared void, (8) certainty and possibility of performance. • Exam line: 'All contracts are agreements, but all agreements are not contracts.' 📐 Formula of the Day – P8 Cost Accounting Stock levels • Re-order level = Maximum usage × Maximum lead time • Minimum level = ROL − (Normal usage × Normal lead time) • Maximum level = ROL + ROQ − (Minimum usage × Minimum lead time) • Average stock level = Minimum level + ½ ROQ (or ½ × (Minimum + Maximum)) 💪 One concept a day = 300+ concepts by exam day. Keep building strong CMA Inter concepts!
2026-11-13.g2: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P9A Operations Management Capacity, utilisation and efficiency • Design capacity = maximum output under ideal conditions. Effective capacity = design capacity less allowances (maintenance, product mix, scheduling). • Utilisation = Actual output ÷ Design capacity. Efficiency = Actual output ÷ Effective capacity. • Efficiency is always ≥ utilisation, because effective capacity is smaller than design capacity. 📐 Formula of the Day – P11A Financial Management Leverages • Operating leverage = Contribution ÷ EBIT • Financial leverage = EBIT ÷ EBT • Combined leverage = Contribution ÷ EBT = OL × FL 💪 One concept a day = 300+ concepts by exam day. Keep building strong CMA Inter concepts!

2026-11-14.g1: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P6 Financial Accounting Fundamental accounting assumptions • AS 1 recognises three fundamental assumptions: Going concern, Consistency and Accrual. • If they are followed, no disclosure is needed. If any one is NOT followed, the fact must be disclosed. • Do not confuse them with the considerations for selecting policies: Prudence, Substance over form and Materiality. ⚖️ Section of the Day – P5 Business Laws Sec 10 – What agreements are contracts • All agreements are contracts if made by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and are not expressly declared void. • Exam use: list these 5 conditions to test whether any agreement is a valid contract. 💪 Future CMA, this is how toppers revise – one clear concept at a time.
2026-11-14.g2: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P10A Corporate Accounting Capital Redemption Reserve (CRR) • Preference shares may be redeemed out of profits available for dividend or out of a fresh issue made for the purpose (Companies Act, 2013 – Sec 55). • When redeemed out of profits, an amount equal to the nominal value redeemed is transferred to CRR. • CRR = Nominal value redeemed − Proceeds of fresh issue. Premium on redemption does not affect CRR. CRR can be used only for issuing fully paid bonus shares. ⚖️ Section of the Day – P10B Auditing Sec 139 – Auditor rotation (Companies Act, 2013) • Listed and prescribed companies: an individual auditor – not more than one term of 5 consecutive years; an audit firm – not more than two terms of 5 consecutive years. • Cooling-off period of 5 years before reappointment. • First auditor of a non-government company is appointed by the Board within 30 days of registration. 💪 Future CMA, this is how toppers revise – one clear concept at a time.

2026-11-16.g1: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P7A Direct Taxation Residential status of an individual • Resident if EITHER: (a) in India for 182 days or more in the previous year, OR (b) 60 days or more in the year AND 365 days or more in the 4 preceding years. • The 60-day condition is replaced by 182 days for an Indian citizen leaving India for employment, and by 120 days for certain Indian citizens/PIOs with high Indian income. • Residential status is decided separately for every year; citizenship is not the test. 📐 Formula of the Day – P6 Financial Accounting Insurance claim with average clause • Claim = Loss of stock × (Policy value ÷ Value of stock on the date of fire) • Applies only when the stock is under-insured (policy value < value of stock). • Value of stock on the date of fire is found by preparing a Memorandum Trading A/c. 💪 Cost, control, compliance – a CMA masters all three. Today you mastered one more concept.
2026-11-16.g2: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P11A Financial Management Operating cycle • Gross operating cycle = Raw material period + WIP period + Finished goods period + Receivables period. • Net operating cycle = Gross operating cycle − Payables (creditors) period. • A shorter net cycle means less working capital is locked up. 📐 Formula of the Day – P12 Management Accounting Material variances • Material cost variance = (SQ × SP) − (AQ × AP) • Material price variance = AQ × (SP − AP) • Material usage variance = SP × (SQ − AQ) • Check: MCV = MPV + MUV 💪 Cost, control, compliance – a CMA masters all three. Today you mastered one more concept.

2026-11-17.g1: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P8 Cost Accounting Elements of cost • Direct material + Direct labour + Direct expenses = Prime cost. • Prime cost + Factory/works overheads = Works (factory) cost; + Administration overheads = Cost of production; + Selling & distribution overheads = Cost of sales. • Cost of sales + Profit = Sales. ⚖️ Section of the Day – P7B Indirect Taxation CGST Sec 8 – Composite and mixed supply • Composite supply → taxed as a supply of the principal supply. • Mixed supply → taxed as a supply of the item attracting the highest rate of tax. • Linked to Day 2 MCQ: laptop + carry bag. 💪 Dec 2026 is calling. Stay consistent, stay CMA-focused!
2026-11-17.g2: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P12 Management Accounting Marginal costing – CVP basics • Contribution = Sales − Variable cost. P/V ratio = Contribution ÷ Sales × 100. • BEP (units) = Fixed cost ÷ Contribution per unit. BEP (₹) = Fixed cost ÷ P/V ratio. • Margin of safety = Actual sales − BEP sales; Profit = Margin of safety × P/V ratio. ⚖️ Section of the Day – P10B Auditing Sec 141 – Who can be an auditor • Only a Chartered Accountant (or a firm where the majority of partners practising in India are CAs) can be appointed as the statutory auditor of a company. • Disqualified: a body corporate (other than an LLP), an officer or employee of the company, a partner or employee of an officer/employee, and persons with specified financial interests or business relationships. • CMA link: cost audit under Sec 148 is done only by a Cost Accountant. 💪 Dec 2026 is calling. Stay consistent, stay CMA-focused!

2026-11-18.g1: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P5 Business Laws Condition vs warranty (Sale of Goods Act) • Condition: a stipulation essential to the main purpose of the contract – breach gives the right to repudiate the contract. • Warranty: a stipulation collateral to the main purpose – breach gives only a claim for damages. • A buyer may waive a condition or elect to treat it as a breach of warranty (Sec 13). 📐 Formula of the Day – P8 Cost Accounting Labour incentive plans • Halsey: Earnings = (TT × R) + 50% × (TA − TT) × R • Rowan: Earnings = (TT × R) + [(TA − TT) ÷ TA] × TT × R • TA = time allowed, TT = time taken, R = rate per hour 💪 Every concept you learn adds value – just like a CMA adds value to every business.
2026-11-18.g2: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P9B Strategic Management Balanced Scorecard • Developed by Robert Kaplan and David Norton (1992). • Four perspectives: Financial, Customer, Internal Business Process, Learning & Growth. • Purpose: link strategy to measures beyond profit, balancing short-term results with long-term capability. 📐 Formula of the Day – P11A Financial Management Capital budgeting • NPV = PV of cash inflows − PV of cash outflows • Profitability index = PV of cash inflows ÷ PV of cash outflows • IRR = the rate at which NPV = 0 (find by interpolation) • Accept if NPV > 0, PI > 1, IRR > cost of capital 💪 Every concept you learn adds value – just like a CMA adds value to every business.

2026-11-19.g1: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P6 Financial Accounting Bills of exchange – due date • Due date = Date of bill + Term + 3 days of grace (Negotiable Instruments Act). • No days of grace for bills payable on demand or at sight. • If the due date is a public holiday, the bill is due on the preceding business day. ⚖️ Section of the Day – P5 Business Laws Sec 11 – Who is competent to contract • A person is competent to contract if he has attained majority, is of sound mind and is not disqualified by any law. • Agreement with a minor = void ab initio (Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose). 💪 Believe in your preparation – the CMA designation rewards consistent effort.
2026-11-19.g2: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P10B Auditing Services an auditor cannot render (Sec 144) • Accounting and book-keeping; internal audit; design and implementation of any financial information system; • Actuarial services; investment advisory services; investment banking services; outsourced financial services; management services. • These are prohibited directly or indirectly – no Board or Audit Committee approval can permit them. ⚖️ Section of the Day – P10A Corporate Accounting Sec 52 – Securities premium • Premium received on issue of shares is transferred to the Securities Premium Account. • It can be used only for specified purposes, such as issuing fully paid bonus shares, writing off preliminary expenses and share/debenture issue expenses, providing premium on redemption of preference shares or debentures, and buy-back of shares. 💪 Believe in your preparation – the CMA designation rewards consistent effort.

2026-11-20.g1: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P7B Indirect Taxation Composite vs mixed supply (GST) • Composite supply: two or more supplies naturally bundled, one being the principal supply – taxed at the rate of the principal supply. • Mixed supply: two or more supplies sold together for a single price but NOT naturally bundled – taxed at the highest rate among them. • Example: laptop with carry bag = composite; gift hamper of sweets, dry fruits and drinks = mixed. 📐 Formula of the Day – P6 Financial Accounting Depreciation • SLM: Depreciation = (Cost − Residual value) ÷ Useful life • WDV: Depreciation = Opening WDV × Rate % • WDV rate = 1 − (Residual value ÷ Cost)^(1/n) 💪 One concept a day = 300+ concepts by exam day. Keep building strong CMA Inter concepts!
2026-11-20.g2: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P11B Business Data Analytics Data, information and knowledge • Data = raw, unprocessed facts (e.g. individual bill entries). • Information = data processed and organised to give meaning (e.g. a daily sales summary). • Knowledge = information applied with experience to take decisions (e.g. deciding stock levels from sales trends). 📐 Formula of the Day – P12 Management Accounting Labour variances • Labour cost variance = (SH × SR) − (AH paid × AR) • Labour rate variance = AH paid × (SR − AR) • Labour efficiency variance = SR × (SH − AH worked) • Idle time variance = Idle hours × SR 💪 One concept a day = 300+ concepts by exam day. Keep building strong CMA Inter concepts!

2026-11-21.g1: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P8 Cost Accounting Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) • EOQ = √(2AO ÷ C), where A = annual demand, O = ordering cost per order, C = carrying cost per unit per year. • At EOQ, total ordering cost = total carrying cost, and total inventory cost is minimum. • Assumes constant demand, constant prices and instant replenishment. ⚖️ Section of the Day – P7B Indirect Taxation CGST Sec 9 – Levy and collection • CGST is levied on intra-State supplies of goods or services, at rates notified on the recommendation of the GST Council (maximum CGST rate 20%). • Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is outside GST. • Sec 9(3): reverse charge on notified supplies; Sec 9(4): reverse charge on notified supplies from unregistered persons to notified registered persons. 💪 Future CMA, this is how toppers revise – one clear concept at a time.
2026-11-21.g2: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P12 Management Accounting Fixed vs flexible budget • Fixed budget: prepared for one level of activity and not changed with the actual level. • Flexible budget: recognises cost behaviour and is prepared for different activity levels. • For control, actual results are compared with a flexible budget at the actual level of activity. ⚖️ Section of the Day – P10B Auditing Sec 143 – Powers and duties of auditors • The auditor has a right of access at all times to the books, accounts and vouchers of the company. • The auditor reports to the members whether the financial statements give a true and fair view. • Sec 143(12): fraud involving ₹1 crore or more must be reported to the Central Government. 💪 Future CMA, this is how toppers revise – one clear concept at a time.

2026-11-23.g1: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P5 Business Laws Private company (Companies Act, 2013) • Sec 2(68): restricts the right to transfer shares, limits members to 200 (excluding employee-members) and prohibits invitation to the public to subscribe to securities. • Minimum 2 members and 2 directors. • Joint holders are treated as a single member. 📐 Formula of the Day – P8 Cost Accounting Overhead absorption • Machine hour rate = Overheads of the machine ÷ Machine hours • Absorbed overheads = Actual base × Pre-determined rate • Under-absorption = Actual overheads − Absorbed overheads (if positive) 💪 Cost, control, compliance – a CMA masters all three. Today you mastered one more concept.
2026-11-23.g2: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P9B Strategic Management SWOT analysis • Strengths and Weaknesses are INTERNAL (resources, capabilities). • Opportunities and Threats are EXTERNAL (market, government, technology, competition). • A new government subsidy for the industry = Opportunity, not Strength. 📐 Formula of the Day – P9A Operations Management Network analysis • PERT expected time te = (to + 4tm + tp) ÷ 6 • Variance = ((tp − to) ÷ 6)² • Total float = LS − ES; Free float = ES (successor) − EF 💪 Cost, control, compliance – a CMA masters all three. Today you mastered one more concept.

2026-11-24.g1: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P6 Financial Accounting SLM vs WDV depreciation • Straight-line method: same amount every year on original cost. • Written down value: fixed % on the opening book value – charge reduces every year. • WDV never reduces the asset to zero; SLM can. ⚖️ Section of the Day – P5 Business Laws Sale of Goods Act Sec 12 – Condition and warranty • Condition: essential to the main purpose – breach allows repudiation. • Warranty: collateral to the main purpose – breach gives damages only. • Whether a stipulation is a condition or warranty depends on the construction of the contract. 💪 Dec 2026 is calling. Stay consistent, stay CMA-focused!
2026-11-24.g2: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P10A Corporate Accounting Earnings per share (AS 20) • Basic EPS = Net profit attributable to equity shareholders ÷ Weighted average equity shares outstanding. • Shares issued or bought back during the year are weighted for the time they were outstanding. • Bonus issue: treated as if issued at the start of the earliest period reported (no time weighting). ⚖️ Section of the Day – P10B Auditing Sec 148 – Cost audit • The Central Government may direct prescribed classes of companies to maintain cost records and get them audited. • The cost auditor must be a Cost Accountant (CMA) in practice, appointed by the Board; remuneration is ratified by the members. • The statutory auditor cannot be appointed as the cost auditor. 💪 Dec 2026 is calling. Stay consistent, stay CMA-focused!

2026-11-25.g1: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P7B Indirect Taxation Customs – assessable value • Based on transaction value (CIF) of the imported goods. • If freight is not ascertainable: 20% of FOB. If insurance is not ascertainable: 1.125% of FOB. • Convert at the exchange rate notified by CBIC on the relevant date. 📐 Formula of the Day – P6 Financial Accounting Average due date • Average due date = Base date ± (Sum of products ÷ Sum of amounts) • Product = Amount × Number of days from the base date • Interest = Amount × Rate × Days ÷ 365 💪 Every concept you learn adds value – just like a CMA adds value to every business.
2026-11-25.g2: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P11A Financial Management Cost of debt • Irredeemable debt: Kd (after tax) = Interest × (1 − tax rate) ÷ Net proceeds. • Use net proceeds (issue price less flotation cost), not face value. • Interest is tax-deductible, so debt is usually the cheapest source of finance. 📐 Formula of the Day – P11A Financial Management Working capital cycle • Raw material period = Average RM stock ÷ RM consumed per day • Debtors period = Average debtors ÷ Credit sales per day • Net operating cycle = RM + WIP + FG + Debtors − Creditors periods 💪 Every concept you learn adds value – just like a CMA adds value to every business.

2026-11-26.g1: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P8 Cost Accounting Normal vs abnormal loss (process costing) • Normal loss: expected, unavoidable – its cost is absorbed by good units; scrap value is credited to the process. • Abnormal loss: loss above the normal level – valued like good units and transferred to Costing P&L A/c. • Abnormal gain: actual loss less than normal – also valued like good units. ⚖️ Section of the Day – P5 Business Laws LLP Act Sec 7 – Designated partners • Every LLP must have at least two designated partners who are individuals. • At least one designated partner must be resident in India (stayed in India for at least 120 days during the financial year). • Linked to Day 5 MCQ. 💪 Believe in your preparation – the CMA designation rewards consistent effort.
2026-11-26.g2: 🧠 Concept of the Day – P12 Management Accounting Activity-based costing (ABC) • Overheads are collected in activity cost pools (e.g. set-ups, inspections, orders). • Each pool is charged to products using a cost driver: Rate = Pool cost ÷ Total driver quantity. • Gives more accurate product costs where overheads are high and products differ in complexity. ⚖️ Section of the Day – P10A Corporate Accounting Sec 68 – Buy-back of shares • Buy-back out of free reserves, securities premium or proceeds of a different issue. • Limit: up to 25% of paid-up capital + free reserves (Board approval up to 10%; above that, special resolution). • Post buy-back debt-equity ratio should not exceed 2 : 1. 💪 Believe in your preparation – the CMA designation rewards consistent effort.

2026-11-27.g1: 📐 Formula of the Day – P8 Cost Accounting Process costing – equivalent units • Equivalent units = Physical units × % of completion • Cost per equivalent unit = Total cost ÷ Equivalent units • Abnormal loss/gain is valued at the same cost per unit as good output 💪 One concept a day = 300+ concepts by exam day. Keep building strong CMA Inter concepts!
2026-11-27.g2: 📐 Formula of the Day – P12 Management Accounting Key factor decision • Contribution per unit of key factor = Contribution per unit ÷ Key factor units per product • Rank products on this ratio, not on contribution per unit. • Key factor = the scarce resource (labour hours, material, machine hours) 💪 One concept a day = 300+ concepts by exam day. Keep building strong CMA Inter concepts!

2026-11-28.g1: ⚖️ Section of the Day – P7B Indirect Taxation CGST Sec 16 – Eligibility for ITC • Conditions: possession of a tax invoice; details of the invoice appear in GSTR-2B; goods/services received; tax actually paid to the Government by the supplier; and return filed. • ITC on an invoice must be taken within the time limit prescribed in Sec 16(4). 💪 Future CMA, this is how toppers revise – one clear concept at a time.
2026-11-28.g2: ⚖️ Section of the Day – P10B Auditing Sec 144 – Prohibited services • Accounting & book-keeping, internal audit, design of financial information systems, actuarial, investment advisory, investment banking, outsourced financial and management services. • No approval can permit these services. 💪 Future CMA, this is how toppers revise – one clear concept at a time.
